note: Bambu Studio applies one parser to every printer model and firmware and detects the shape at runtime. Do not branch on model id.

keys.comment: Each entry carries its own id; 255 = main slot, 254 = deputy slot.
The id reported by the printer is discarded and the slot is treated as the main slot (255). The A1 reports "id": "254" here but is still the main slot.

slot_presence.note: Whether a slot holds a spool comes from ams.tray_exist_bits, not from the per-tray `state` value: Bambu Studio never reads `state`. Bit `tray_index` of tray_exist_bits is the `is_exists` flag for that slot.

exist_bits.comment: Hex strings. Bit N of tray_exist_bits is set when tray index N holds a spool; bit N of ams_exist_bits when AMS N is attached.

ams_type.comment: The AMS `info` field is a hex string; these bits hold the DevAmsType. Entries without `info` use the default.

tray_index.comment: From DevAms::GetTrayId. AMS types missing here have no mapping in Bambu Studio either (it asserts and returns -1), so treat their slots as present rather than reading a meaningless bit.

slot_count.comment: From DevAms::GetSlotCount. AMS types not listed report as many slots as the printer sent trays for.

filament_info_known.comment: DevAmsTray::is_tray_info_ready. A slot that exists but reports no tray_type holds a spool whose filament the AMS has not identified; its settings can still be written.

state_field.comment: Observed from printer output, NOT from Bambu Studio, which ignores this field. Use only as a fallback when the printer reports trays but no tray_exist_bits.

rfid_identity.note: Whether the printer identified a slot's filament itself comes from ams.ams[].tray[].tag_uid, which only an RFID read can fill in. The ams_filament_setting command has no tag_uid field, so a hand-set slot can never look auto-detected.

auto_detected.rule: tag_uid is present and not every character is '0'
auto_detected.comment: DevFilaSystem::IsBBL_Filament. Studio inverts this into m_is_third, the flag behind its third-party filament UI.

official_tag.comment: A genuine Bambu tag; tray_uuid then holds the per-spool serial Studio treats as that spool's identity. Other tags still prove a read happened, but carry no usable serial.

not_a_source.tray_is_bbl_bits: Despite the name this tracks occupancy, not Bambu-ness: it was observed reading 'f' on a P2S with one tagged slot of four, and matching tray_exist_bits exactly on an A1. Bambu Studio parses it (DevFilaSystem.cpp) but only ever compares it against its previous value to detect change. Do not use it to decide whether a spool was auto-detected — use tag_uid.

slot_read_state.note: A slot whose bit is clear in tray_read_done_bits, or set in tray_reading_bits, is one the AMS has not finished reading. Both are indexed by slot_presence.tray_index, like tray_exist_bits.
slot_read_state.pending_rule: reading bit set, or read_done bit clear, for this slot's tray index
slot_read_state.comment: Bambu Studio parses both masks but only compares them against their previous values to detect change (StatusPanel's last_tray_is_bbl_bits and friends); it does not refuse writes during a read. Using them to gate a write is therefore an extension, not upstream behaviour, and is based on observed printer output: on an A1 and a P2S both masks cleared and restored across every tag read observed, and read_done matched tray_exist_bits exactly at rest. Treat unparseable or absent masks as 'not pending' so a printer that omits them keeps working.

physical_ams.ams_id: the 0-based AMS id as reported in push_status
physical_ams.slot_id: the 0-based tray id as reported in push_status
